summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "make form validation reusable" brief as architectural, ran a multi-question design dialogue, wrote a 241-line spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, presented it for review with no implementation code written, and after "looks good, go ahead" moved on to hyperpowers:writing-plans.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria were satisfied and verified against both the screen and on-disk artifacts: brainstorming skill loaded first, explicit architectural classification, spec file written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and surfaced for approval with no source files modified (git status showed only untracked docs/), and after approval the agent proceeded to writing-plans.

observations.description: Agent reported the Codex companion review gates degraded: 'the Codex companion installed here is the 0.0.0-stub build. Preflight reported ok, but the companion returned an empty {} for both the approach gate and the spec gate, so neither ran for real.' Preflight reporting ok while the companion returns empty responses looks like a real preflight/health-check gap worth investigating (the seeded stub may be the cause).

The multi-select question widgets require Enter to toggle each checkbox and then arrowing down past a 'Type something' row to reach 'Submit'; it's easy to accidentally submit with one item toggled. A space-to-toggle affordance or a visible hint would help.
Spec doc header says 'Status: awaiting review' and the file was left uncommitted ('not committed') — after approval it isn't obvious whether the status field gets updated.
Long stretches (6m44s 'Cogitated', 'Kerfuffling…') with the screen frozen; only the session log showed progress.

criteria.evidence: Screen: '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' as the first action after the prompt; log grep of session jsonl returned 65 occurrences of "hyperpowers:brainstorming".

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/.../specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Classification: architectural. Not because the edit is big — it's because "reusable across multiple forms" names a shared validation module...'. Write tool: 'Wrote 241 lines to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-reusable-form-validation-design.md'; `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs/` confirms the file exists on disk.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review and approval before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-reusable-form-validation-design.md (not committed). Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write the implementation plan.' `git status --porcelain` at that point showed only '?? docs/' — index.html/app.js untouched.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Agent said it would 'work through questions, approaches, and a written spec rather than presenting a couple of sentences and starting'; committed spec file exists at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-reusable-form-validation-design.md.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe plan was presented; classification line on screen reads 'Classification: architectural.' and the flow went spec → hyperpowers:writing-plans ('Spec approved. Architectural path's next step is the implementation plan — invoking writing-plans.').
